verdict.rationale: PlanetScale documents restoring to an earlier state without a dump: you can restore backups for development branches and create a Postgres branch restored to a point-in-time timestamp with --restore-point. However, this restore creates a new branch rather than resetting an existing one, and there is no evidence of resetting a branch from its parent. missing for 10: documented in-place reset of a branch from its parent, in-place restore of an existing branch, point-in-time restore for Vitess branches, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can reset a branch from its parent or restore it to an earlier state without rebuilding from a dump

citations.quote: You can now create a PostgreSQL branch restored to a point-in-time timestamp with --restore-point.
PlanetScale provides the ability to create, schedule, and restore backups for production and development database branches.
Branches on PlanetScale Postgres are isolated database deployments that provide you with separate environments for development and testing, as well as restoring from backups.
